tips:
• Use freshly drawn water brought just off the rolling boil (around 95°C).
• Pre-warm your teapot or mug with hot water before adding leaves.
• Cover with a lid during steeping to trap delicate volatile aromatic oils.
• Strain promptly after 4 minutes; over-steeping releases bitter tannins.

• Never use boiling water; allow kettle to cool for 3–4 minutes down to 80°C.
• Boiling water scalds delicate green leaves and causes harsh astringency.
• Steep gently for 3 minutes for sweet vegetal and floral sweetness.
• Ceylon green leaves can be re-steeped a second time for 2 minutes.

• Heat fresh filtered spring water to approximately 85°C.
• Use a generous tablespoon since fluffy white tea leaves have higher volume.
• Allow 5 full minutes to gently release mild melon and peach notes.
• White tea leaves can comfortably yield up to 3 infusions.

• Brew in clear glassware or white porcelain to admire the vertical standing buds.
• Keep water temperature steady at 85°C to avoid scorching downy bud tips.
• Give the dense unopened needles a generous 5 minutes to slowly unfurl.
• Savour without milk, sugar, or citrus to enjoy pure honeydew nectar.
